text:
For an **overnight pellet-smoker cook**, I’d choose the **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2**. Its 2,073.6 Wh capacity and 2,600 W inverter give plenty of headroom for startup, and the cited estimate is two or three 12-hour cooks per charge—useful if you’ll also charge campsite devices. [Details and purchase link](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)

For a lighter, lower-cost option, the **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (1,070 Wh, 1,500 W) is estimated to handle one overnight cook. A pellet grill typically draws about 35–60 W after ignition, but the igniter can briefly need 200–400 W, so check your grill’s label and the station’s surge rating. [Sizing and model details](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)

These recommendations are for **pellet grills**, not electric smokers with a heating element. Those can draw around 1,000 W continuously and need a much larger station for an overnight run. [Electric-smoker sizing](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-smoker/)
